delivery_lane.mac_lane_correction_note: 2026-09-05, second correction. This first read ship-warden-multi-host, then hybrid-mac-warden-linux-root-installer with mac: ship-warden. The second was still wrong and this seat wrote it: Ship Warden's membership gate is COMPONENT-level, not platform-level — daemon.ts refuses on componentHome before any target is considered — so the warden refuses this package on the Mac exactly as it refuses it on Linux, and declaring mac: ship-warden repeated the same defect this contract was repaired to remove: naming a lane that cannot fire. Both platforms now name a component-owned installer, which is what SHAPE-2026-08-17 decision test 3 prescribes for a component that is not warden-shippable. module-installer is an existing controlled-vocabulary value (system-prompt-append declares it); no new value was invented.
delivery_lane.lane_change_note: 2026-09-05: was ship-warden-multi-host. That value had exactly one declarer (this contract) and no implementation — the running warden daemon contains zero occurrences of ship-warden-multi-host, remote-root-daemon, delivery_lane, or the host twr, so the lane could never execute even with workspace membership granted. Switched to the only lane kind proven to reach the tower (throughline-provider-broker uses it). Per SHAPE-2026-08-17 decision test 3, a component that is not warden-shippable keeps its prior lane until wardenized. Decision record: /Users/Admin/core-root/vault/01_Projects/workbench/infra/t3code/_meta/Decision-ThroughLine-Desktop-Delivery-Lane-2026-09-05.html
delivery_lane.linux_privilege_note: The kind name is the existing controlled vocabulary value and says 'root'; this component's Linux target needs none. Measured 2026-09-05 on twr: sudo requires a password, /srv/throughline is writable by twr, and the server unit is a --user service in twr's own home. The installer still carries the privilege gate below its checks for any future target that does need it.

targets.install_path_note: {version} is substituted from version_source at install time. It was hard-coded to 0.0.37 until 2026-09-05, which silently went stale on every release; the installer refuses rather than guessing if substitution yields a path that does not match the built artifact.
targets.launcher_note: The desktop icon runs this script, not the AppImage, and it is the only place three host-level facts are handed to the window: the shared data directory so the app and the background service use ONE database, the stop-and-restart handoff of the background service so two servers never hit that database at once, and the durable queue address plus the provider address read out of the service unit. Added to this contract 2026-09-21 because the lockstep publish step launched current_link DIRECTLY, bypassing all three. Measured that day on the tower: the process actually serving port 3773 carries the queue address only when it is started through this launcher.

parent_module_impact.summary: This contract consolidates the already-proven lockstep desktop targets into the desktop component without changing application behavior.
parent_module_impact.no_impact_rationale: The target set, artifact names, install addresses, and all-required completion rule already governed the lockstep lane; this move removes the parallel contract.
